narrative.northStar: A capable companion, with the details in reach.
narrative.overview: Hutch is a personal assistant for everyday work. People begin in a conversation, turn a request into a specialist when useful, and review important actions in plain language. Model, integration, memory, and execution details are available when someone wants to adjust them. The design job is helpful at first glance, dependable when it matters: make the next useful step obvious without hiding what a service can access or what the machine has actually confirmed.
keyCharacteristics: Familiar chat and app patterns carry everyday tasks; advanced controls appear in clear, optional layers instead of defining the first impression. Activity hides empty buckets and offers one clear state with links to chat and past work.
Assistant settings lead with the editable name and short role; standing directions and advanced controls stay under one clearly labeled customization layer.

A simple, shape-aware 2D character gives the app a recognizable face. Each distinct silhouette has a fitted dark-green face panel with two narrow, curved light slits; contour, spacing, height, and tilt adapt to the usable face area. Keep the face free of pupils, highlights, or detached marks. Larger original 3D character art belongs to marketing.

Provider artwork follows current published rules by context. ChatGPT uses OpenAI’s exact, unaltered white Blossom beside its explicit name. Microsoft Outlook, Gmail, and Google Calendar use original category glyphs beside their full names unless Hutch receives permission for specific product marks. No provider mark is recolored or fetched remotely.

Layered graphite surfaces keep long sessions comfortable. Emerald is the brand and primary action; azure is interaction; amber means a person needs to act; rose means failure. Text and familiar icons reinforce each color’s meaning.
Display, page, and section headings use locally bundled Archivo; interface prose and instructions use system sans, and mono is reserved for measured values such as IDs, durations, and budgets.

rules.name: The Measure Rule
rules.body: Reading text caps at ~72ch; anything wider is layout debt.

rules.name: The One-Ink Rule
rules.body: Emerald fills always carry near-black ink (#052e21); white on emerald is forbidden (≈2.5:1).

rules.name: The Amber Rule
rules.body: Amber appears only where a person must act now — pending approvals, expiring deadlines under two minutes, the attention nav badge. Never as decoration, never on "done" or "failed".

rules.name: The Scale Rule
rules.body: Every corner radius comes from `rounded.*`; no ad-hoc values.

rules.name: The Measured Rule
rules.body: Mono type is only for values the server measured — never for prose, labels, or marketing.

dos: Keep motion short, functional and tied to an actual state change; honour reduced motion and the Reduce effects override.
Take every radius from `rounded.*`; keep the pill only for chips.
Pair every icon with a word for state; give every control a visible focus ring.
Use mono only for machine-measured values.
Show real server state: if the API cannot confirm it, say "unknown".
donts: Never put white on emerald, or amber on something that isn't person-needed.
Never box tool calls, or wrap decided approvals in cards.
Never run ambient loops, pulsing dots on idle state, or animated backgrounds behind work.
Never show a count, status or receipt the server did not produce.
Never add a radius outside the scale, or a colour outside the palette.
